scene6_choice1_option2_screen8.text: They don’t talk about last night. Not directly. But it’s there — in the pauses, the way her fingers brush the edge of her cup, the way he keeps looking at her like he’s afraid to blink and miss something.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen9.text: You always this charming before breakfast?

scene6_choice1_option2_screen10.text: Only with people I want to see again.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen13.text: She finishes her coffee, sets the cup down with quiet finality. Then reaches into her purse and pulls out a pen.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen14.text: (matter-of-fact) Here. So you don’t have to guess next time you’re bored and wondering if I was real.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen15.text: She writes her number on the back of the café receipt. Tears it off and hands it to him.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen16.text: Don’t lose it. I don’t repeat detours.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen17.text: (accepting it carefully, like it’s something fragile) I won’t. (pauses) Does this mean I get to text you weird thoughts at 2 a.m.?

scene6_choice1_option2_screen19.text: They step outside. The street is busier now. She looks toward the taxi already waiting, engine idling. Then back at him.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen20.text: (soft) Thanks. For... letting me be someone else for a while.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen21.text: She kisses him on the cheek — barely there, barely not — and gets into the cab.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen22.text: He watches as it drives away, the city swallowing her up like a secret. He folds the receipt once, then slides it carefully into the cover of his passport — like a stamp he doesn’t want to lose.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen23.text: Their unexpected evening may have ended, but their story hasn´t.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Ethan doesn’t say a word. He just finishes packing — methodically, like it's easier to focus on zippers than on her.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen2.text: Melena watches him from across the room. Waiting. Expecting a pitch. A reason. One more line he might toss her way like a rope. But it never comes.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen3.text: (quietly) You’re not going to convince me?

scene6_choice1_option3_screen4.text: (shrugging, but his voice is warm) You’re too smart for that. I don’t want to push you. But I do want you to want to stay.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen5.text: She exhales through her nose. Walks to the window. The city outside is soft with morning gold, the streets still quiet, the world suspended in a moment that could go either way.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen6.text: Her reflection meets her eyes — still a little tousled, still someone she doesn’t entirely recognize. Or maybe someone she’s just meeting again. She turns. Calm. Collected. A decision behind her gaze.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen7.text: (gently) I’m heading to the airport. But if you really want to talk again… (pauses, glancing at the door) You can ask the front desk for my number.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen8.text: She crosses the room, her bag slung over one shoulder. Stops in front of him. He doesn’t move — doesn’t dare. She leans in and brushes a kiss against his cheek. Barely there. But everything in it.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen10.text: And just like that, she’s gone.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen11.text: Ethan exhales a breath he didn’t know he was holding. As the tram bell rings down the street and the scent of pastries drifts through the morning air.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen12.text: Their unexpected evening may have ended, but their story hasn´t.
